explanation: Fires in source code on the name of a newly declared/assigned variable or function parameter, i.e. the identifier right after a type, 'var/const', 'function(', or at line start before '=' (e.g. 'log = logging.getLogger', 'MyMesh mesh;', 'function(event)'). Weak on other identifiers in code, near zero in prose.

Diffuse: fires on assorted mid-phrase tokens with no clear shared feature, including the space in legal reporter citations ('F.3d 1420'), thousands-separator commas in numbers, and random words in prose or code comments.

Fires in the import/include/require header at the top of a code file: on 'import', 'use', '#include' pieces, header-file suffixes like '.h', and the separators between consecutive import lines. Weak elsewhere in code and in prose.

Fires on 'home' (and similar place/role nouns such as 'work', 'duty', 'job', 'life') after a possessive or a movement/location verb, as in 'their home', 'returned home', 'go to work', 'at his home'. Moderate on possessive pronouns and other personal nouns; weak elsewhere.

Mixed: fires on 'and' in 'before and after' / comparison pairs, 'same'/'second'/'true' in comparison phrasing, 'sender' in C# event handlers, the '-' in '[@B1-ijerph' citation keys, and assorted scientific word pieces. No single shared feature.

Fires on the word that starts a capitalized proper-name phrase, mostly 'the' in 'United States District Court for the [Southern] District of ...' and 'Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit'. Also moderate on the first word inside other fixed names like 'Seven Against Thebes', 'Old Spanish Trail', 'New World', 'Big Five'.

Fires on function words or verbs that link a noun to its complement in formal, academic or legal writing, e.g. 'in' in 'rights in', 'effect(s) of', 'in part', 'relating to', 'affecting', 'retain', 'free of charge, to'. Strongest in abstracts and license or legal boilerplate; weak in casual prose.

Fires on tokens near the start of a document or code file, especially copyright/license headers ('Copyright ©', 'Copyright 2011', '2016 The Chromium Authors', '@license') and opening declarations ('public function __construct', 'public static void'). Also hits some opening question words ('How can', 'When is'). Weak elsewhere.

Fires on an opening quotation mark (" or “ or ') that begins a quoted term or name after a naming verb or preposition, as in 'called "', 'known as "', 'words like "', 'defined as “'. Closing quotes and quotes opening dialogue are weak.

Fires on 'that' after a noun, starting a content or relative clause, especially after nouns of information or claim ('evidence that', 'a message that', 'a theory that', 'a proposal that'). Weaker for 'that' after verbs or in generic relative clauses; little else fires.

Fires on the word that introduces who did, said or judged something: agentive 'by' after passive verbs ('recognized by', 'condemned by', 'announced by') and attribution verbs like 'says'/'warns' after a quoted claim ('..., says Met Office'). Also 'spokesman for' and 'rating from'.

Fires on a later subword piece or second word of a multi-token proper name or rare word, where the next piece is predictable once the start is seen ('Prime Minister', 'undefeated', 'stackpath', 'org.jetbrains', 'Taliban', 'amnesia', 'antagonists'). Common words weak.
No clear pattern: fires on a heterogeneous mix of subword pieces ('DOOH', 'neuropathic', 'Mogollon'), 'help', 'of', numbers and code tokens, with nothing shared in token or context.

Fires on the backslash starting a LaTeX command inside math mode ('$\lambda', '{\sqrt', '_{\mathfrak'), also on '\' in regexes ('\W'). Small moderate offshoot on mid-word pieces of foreign or technical words.

Fires on joiner punctuation inside compound words or names: the hyphen in 'now-destroyed', 'super-elite', 'US-Präsidenten' and in URL slugs, French elided apostrophes (l'), the Japanese middle dot, '+' in URLs, and ' *)' in Objective-C signatures. Also on broken multibyte Devanagari pieces.

Fires on a word's first piece where a continuation is strongly expected: the start of a multi-token word ('asc|ends', 'occ|uring', 'enc|odes', 'prev|ails', 'Secret|ariat') and mid-sentence pieces in Japanese text. Moderate on head nouns in compounds.

Fires on items in lists or enumerations, mainly a later item or the separator before it: 'and'/'&' joining the last items of a list, list commas, enum values ('TWO', 'D3'), number sequences, and fields in code object literals.

Fires on the first subword piece of a word in non-English Latin-script text (Portuguese, Czech, French, German, Slovene, Romanian) or of a rare proper name or all-caps word ('PMDB-RJ', 'TACOMA', 'ASSAULT'). Common English words are weak.

No coherent pattern: fires on a varied set of tokens, often the second part of compounds or set phrases ('Air pollution', 'liquid crystal', 'External links', 'Horrorcon', 'TABLE OF CONTENTS'), plus 'above', 'ourselves', assembly 'push'.

Fires on the main verb or subject that comes right after the framing opener of a scientific abstract: 'we' in 'Here, we report/show', 'is'/'was' in 'The aim/objective of this paper is', 'has been studied/considered'. Also some unrelated hits ('FHA', 'Social Security').

Fires on 'sleep' and its forms ('sleeping', 'sleeps', 'asleep', 'Sleep'), in prose, medical text and code (thread sleep(), sleep_on). Weakly on 'think'/'dream' and other mental-state or bedtime words.
